protagonist.who: You are an ex-soldier who has spent three years making small, clean lies for large, nervous men, and now you stand at the frontier’s edge with your partner, a borrowed crown in one hand and a sword in the other.
protagonist.history: You met your partner in a garrison where you both learned that a uniform is a mask and a salute is a promise; after the army let you go, you sold false titles in three ports and finally found a country no Englishman had claimed.
protagonist.wants: to cross the frontier and make yourselves its kings before the rival’s authority arrives
protagonist.need: to find out whether the partnership can hold a kingdom, or whether the kingdom will make one of you a subject
protagonist.can_do: bluff, command, divide the visible symbols of power, and keep the con moving from one audience to the next
protagonist.cannot_do: make the local chiefs accept you without a shared performance, or keep the rival’s claim out of the room without your partner’s matching authority

ties.what: the other ex-soldier, the one who can hold a salute as long as you can hold a silence, and the only person whose name is on the contract
the man who knows the passes and knows exactly what you are, and who has chosen to walk with you anyway
the agent of a distant government who wears the government’s sash and who has already taken a chair at your table

protagonist.open: whether you keep the crown shared, or take it alone and let the partnership pay for it
protagonist.name: Bedwyr Ravel

arena.description: A wild, uncharted frontier country: a chain of mountain passes, a swollen river valley, and a makeshift capital camp where the chiefs gather before the season turns.

pressure.description: The rival claimant’s caravan is coming down the river, and the chiefs will make their choice at the autumn banquet; after that, the country will have one authority, and it will not be yours unless the con is finished.
pressure.clock_or_stock: none tracked; the season is told through the rival’s approach and the chiefs’ gatherings, because 3-0c names no failure

opposition.who_or_what: the rival claimant, an agent of a distant government
opposition.wants: to be recognized as the lawful authority over the country, or to install a single king who will answer to his government
opposition.means: he comes with a chain of interpreters, a small armed escort, the government’s red sash, and the power to name one of you king and the other commander before the chiefs
opposition.shown_by: at the dusty waystation where the two of you make the claim, he takes the spare chair, drinks from the third cup, and sits down as if he were already one of the claimants

events.what: At the first chief’s camp, the warriors fall silent when you give a military salute, and the rival claimant steps out of the shadows wearing the distant government’s red sash, making the first audience a test of which authority is believed.
The river swells after the mountain rain, and the crossing becomes a fight with the current; on the far bank the rival’s officer waits with the boat and the government’s escort.

The capital’s makeshift hall is raised with a throne of salvaged wagon wheels and a flag of patched sailcloth; the rival claimant walks in with the government’s escort and names one of you king and the other commander before the chiefs.

mediation.question: How do you divide the crown and the cost between you and your partner: keep the partnership equal, let one of you bear the risk, or break the partnership to secure the kingdom?

to_reach_pole_a.pole: shared kingship: the crown is held by both, and the cost is shared
to_reach_pole_a.what_you_must_do: divide the visible symbols of power so that neither man can be mistaken for the sole king: let your partner hold the sword and the salute, take the crown and the chiefs’ cup, and at the banquet let the chiefs see two men who answer to each other
to_reach_pole_a.cost: both of you bear the frontier’s hardship and the rival’s challenge, and the crown is split and harder to defend; if one falters, the other pays

to_reach_pole_b.pole: sole kingship: one man holds the crown, and the other bears the risk
to_reach_pole_b.what_you_must_do: concentrate authority in one person: take the rival’s chair and the chiefs’ cup, or let your partner stand at the king’s shoulder as commander, and set the other down from the shared seat so he becomes the king’s man
to_reach_pole_b.cost: the partnership is broken or costed; the other becomes a subject, a servant, or the bearer of the blame, and the con becomes a one-man throne

levers: the contract made at the frontier’s edge
the sword and the salute, the visible halves of the claim
the local guide, who knows the truth and can choose which man to trust
the rival claimant’s chair at the chiefs’ table, which lets him name one of you king and the other commander
the chiefs’ cup, which can crown one man or two

price.what: the partner’s place at the shared table, given up when the rival names one king and the other commander, leaving him a subject in the kingdom he helped make
price.why_final: the naming is done before the chiefs with the rival’s chair and the shared cup between you, and once the shared seat is given up, he cannot be bought back into the crown

setups.plant: at the dusty waystation, the rival claimant takes the spare chair, drinks from the third cup, and the notary sets a sword and a crown before you as the two halves of the claim
setups.payoff: at the banquet, the rival takes the spare chair and names one of you king and the other commander, forcing the choice: one king and one commander, or two kings who must share the cost

setups.plant: the local guide keeps his hand on the rim of the shared cup when the chiefs speak, as if he is holding the two of you together
setups.payoff: at the crossing, he is the one who grips your partner’s shoulder in the current, and the chiefs see it

rules.thing: the contract made at the frontier’s edge
rules.terms: the two men who make the contract shall go into the country as two kings; each shall keep the other’s hand in every public audience: one holds the sword, the other the salute; neither may sit alone at the chiefs’ table; if one takes the crown alone, the other stands at his shoulder as commander and yields the shared seat; if the crown is shared, neither may refuse the other’s order in a public ceremony
rules.if_broken: if one takes the crown alone, the other loses his shared seat and his share of the tribute, and becomes the king’s man; the partnership is costed, not the player lost

turns.situation: At the first chief's camp the warriors fall silent when your partner gives the military salute, and the rival claimant steps out of the shadows wearing the distant government's red sash.
turns.what_you_must_do: get the first chief to seat you two as claimants before the rival's sash takes the room

ways_through.way: the chief seats you because your partner gives the salute and you answer with the old army's drill, and the local guide says it is a challenge of officers
ways_through.cost: the rival claimant's interpreter copies the drill, and your partner's salute becomes the claim's face from that night on

ways_through.way: the chief seats you because you let the local guide take the chief's cup and pour for both of you as if you were his guests
ways_through.cost: the local guide keeps his hand on the cup's rim, and the rival claimant drinks from the third cup and sits down as a claimant

turns.set_piece: the first audience in the chief's camp, the salute answered by silence, the rival's red sash in the firelight

turns.situation: The river swells after the mountain rain, and the crossing becomes a fight with the current; on the far bank the rival claimant's officer waits with the boat and the government's escort.
turns.what_you_must_do: get the contract, the sword, and your partner across before the rival's officer takes the boat

ways_through.way: the contract and your partner cross because the local guide takes the boat's stern and your partner grips your shoulder in the current, and the chiefs on the bank see the guide holding your partner's shoulder
ways_through.cost: the local guide's hand is cut on the rope, and he will not leave your partner's side after, choosing to trust him more than you

ways_through.way: the contract and your partner cross because you let the rival claimant's officer give you the boat's rope and name the crossing a government survey
ways_through.cost: the officer's escort takes the contract's seal for the night, and your partner is made to stand in the current in the government's shadow

ways_through.way: the contract and your partner cross because you and your partner wade the rapid without the boat, each holding the other's shoulder, and the local guide carries the contract in his coat
ways_through.cost: the contract is water-damaged and your partner's shoulder is bruised, and the rival claimant's officer takes the boat for his escort, buying you a day but making the chiefs watch the rival wade too

turns.set_piece: the river crossing where the current is too strong for the boat, the two men wading into the freezing water, their hands gripping the other's shoulders with desperate strength

turns.situation: In the private quarters of the 'kings' the map is spread on a crate between you, the candle flame flickering, and the rival claimant's officer has the contract's seal in his hand and will not say what he will name when the hall opens.
turns.what_you_must_do: keep the contract's terms from becoming the rival's weapon before the hall opens

ways_through.way: you keep the terms hidden because you and your partner agree to hold the sword and the salute as one visible half, and the local guide carries the contract's seal in his own coat
ways_through.cost: the local guide now knows which of you he is keeping safe, and he will answer him first when the chiefs speak

ways_through.way: you keep the terms hidden because you give the rival claimant's officer the contract's seal in exchange for his word that he will name both of you in the chiefs' hearing
ways_through.cost: the officer's word is the government's word, and your partner must stand in the current of the rival's naming before the chiefs can see you

turns.set_piece: the two partners standing in a narrow tent at night, the map spread on a crate between them, the candle flame flickering as they argue in low voices about who holds the seal and who holds the sword

turns.situation: The capital's makeshift hall is raised with a throne of salvaged wagon wheels and a flag of patched sailcloth, and the rival claimant walks in with the government's escort and names one of you king and the other commander before the chiefs.
turns.what_you_must_do: make the chiefs see who holds the crown in the new hall before the rival's naming is done

ways_through.way: the chiefs see two kings because you and your partner take the chiefs' cup together and the local guide hands the sword to the chief's son, and the rival claimant is made to wait on the spare chair
ways_through.cost: the rival claimant's escort stands with the government's sash at the hall's door, and both of you must answer to the chiefs' questions in public

ways_through.way: the chiefs see one king because you take the rival claimant's chair and drink from the chiefs' cup alone, and your partner stands at your shoulder with the sword
ways_through.cost: your partner loses his shared seat and his share of the tribute, and becomes the king's man

ways_through.way: the chiefs see one king because your partner takes the rival claimant's chair and drinks from the chiefs' cup alone, and you stand at his shoulder with the sword
ways_through.cost: you lose your shared seat and your share of the tribute, and become the king's man

turns.set_piece: a banquet in a makeshift hall where local leaders eat roasted meat and drink fermented spirits, watching the two men with a mix of awe and suspicion, while the men carefully manage their plates to appear sovereign rather than hungry

turns.situation: At the autumn banquet the chiefs' cup is between you, the rival claimant holds the spare chair, and the contract's terms are now the only thing standing between two kings and one subject.
turns.what_you_must_do: settle whose hand is on the shared cup when the chiefs drink

ways_through.way: the chiefs drink from a shared cup because you and your partner take the cup together and the local guide sets the sword and the crown between you, and the rival claimant is left with the spare chair
ways_through.cost: both of you bear the frontier's hardship and the rival's challenge, and the crown is split and harder to defend; if one falters, the other pays

ways_through.way: the chiefs drink from one king's cup because you take the rival claimant's chair and drink from the chiefs' cup alone, and your partner stands at your shoulder with the sword
ways_through.cost: your partner's place at the shared table is given up, and he is a subject in the kingdom he helped make

complications.description: The local guide has been keeping his hand on the rim of the shared cup when the chiefs speak, as if he is holding the two of you together, and at the crossing he is the one who grips your partner's shoulder in the current, and the chiefs see it.

The rival claimant's officer has the contract's seal in his hand and will not say what he will name when the hall opens, and the seal is the only thing that can make the chiefs hear the government's word before yours.

The rival claimant has taken the spare chair at the chiefs' table, drinks from the third cup, and sits down as if he were already one of the claimants, and his chair is the only thing that can name one of you king and the other commander.

cast_seeds.wants: to see which of the white men can hold a silence long enough to be believed
cast_seeds.holds: the warriors' silence and the first chief's cup, which validates the claim
cast_seeds.edge: has seen empires rise and fall in the span of a generation and is amused by the speed of your bluff
cast_seeds.tie: is the first audience to judge the partnership's performance
cast_seeds.voice: speaks in short, heavy sentences that land like stones: 'The salute is a promise. The promise is a debt.'
cast_seeds.name: Godric Corvane

cast_seeds.wants: to hold the sword and the salute, and to be the one who does not flinch when the con wobbles
cast_seeds.holds: the military discipline that makes the salute look real, and the only name on the contract
cast_seeds.edge: resents you for the crown but is the one who checks your rigging every night and will not let you fall
cast_seeds.tie: taught you to lift the summer you came, and expected to be named instead of you
cast_seeds.voice: lifts something heavy while he talks, so he need not look at you: 'She'd have held that pole. You'd need six of me.'
cast_seeds.breaking_point: leaves the night you tell the company what his aunt could not see
cast_seeds.name: Eamon Underhay

cast_seeds.wants: to know which of you will pay for the passes when the river rises
cast_seeds.holds: the knowledge of the passes and the exact moment the bluff becomes a lie
cast_seeds.edge: knows exactly what you are and has chosen to walk with you anyway, which costs him more than the gold
cast_seeds.tie: owes you his life from the garrison, but owes the river his loyalty
cast_seeds.voice: counts the steps while he talks, as if the ground might give way: 'One, two, hands. One, two, hands. You're thinking of selling the horses, aren't you.'
cast_seeds.breaking_point: walks the horses to the riding school the night you sell the first one
cast_seeds.name: Niall Fairhollow

cast_seeds.wants: to be recognized as the lawful authority over the country, or to install a single king who will answer to his government
cast_seeds.holds: the government's red sash and the power to name one of you king and the other commander
cast_seeds.edge: was the founder's first partner, and still keeps her spangled cape in his wagon
cast_seeds.tie: promised the founder he would look after her nephew
cast_seeds.voice: admires everything he means to buy: 'Lovely act. Lovely. Wasted on a field like this.'
cast_seeds.name: Dag Callow

cast_seeds.wants: to secure the seal on the contract before the hall opens, so the naming is done
cast_seeds.holds: the contract's seal and the boat at the swollen river
cast_seeds.edge: is the one who actually checks the rigging, and will not let the rival claimant make a mistake
cast_seeds.tie: owes the rival claimant his commission, but owes the contract its integrity
cast_seeds.voice: speaks in precise, clipped commands that leave no room for argument: 'The seal is in my hand. The seal does not lie.'
cast_seeds.breaking_point: leaves the night you take the agent's money
cast_seeds.name: Fergal Pellam
